text: If a model sees only a handful of positives, it has little to learn from. Resampling rebalances the training data so the rare class gets attention: throw away majority rows, that's undersampling; copy minority rows, that's oversampling; or invent new ones, that's SMOTE. All three are easy to do wrong, so this lesson is about doing them safely.

On our training split, three thousand five hundred fifty-three negatives face only one hundred ninety-seven positives. Undersampling drops negatives down to one hundred ninety-seven each. SMOTE instead grows the positives up to three thousand five hundred fifty-three, by picking a minority row's nearest neighbors and placing a new point on the line between them.

Here's the trap. Resample the whole training set, then cross-validate: recall hits ninety-eight percent, precision ninety-nine point five. It looks nearly perfect. Resample inside each fold instead, the correct way, and recall drops to eighty-eight point eight, precision to ninety-one point three. Average precision alone falls from point nine nine nine to point nine two seven.

Why the gap? Synthetic points are built from real ones, so resampling before splitting leaves near-copies of training rows inside the validation fold. The fix is imblearn's own Pipeline, not scikit-learn's: it runs the sampler only during fit, and predict skips it. You never resample the test set.

Compared honestly on a held-out test set with a random forest: no resampling scores sixty-nine point seven recall at one hundred percent precision. Undersampling jumps recall to eighty-four point eight but drops precision to sixty-eight point three. SMOTE lands between the two, eighty point three recall, ninety-three precision. Average precision barely moves across all five strategies, so resampling mostly slides the model along its existing curve.

Three cautions: encode categoricals before SMOTE, since it interpolates between numeric neighbors, or use SMOTENC for mixed data. Scale features first if they differ wildly. And SMOTE can synthesize points inside noisy, overlapping regions, blurring the class boundary.
Resampling trades precision for recall, and the honest comparison happens inside cross-validation, never outside it. Next: class weights, a lighter alternative to resampling.
